comparison: Perfect agreement on SP measurement findings (C53-C58). Both evaluations find the quantitative SP data across genotypes and bristle types convincing, with appropriate validation through RNAi and rescue experiments. Peer reviewers explicitly note the SP measurements support the authors' conclusions.

Perfect agreement on ectopic HCN expression experiments (C76-C79, C82-C83). Both evaluations support the gain-of-function data showing dose-dependent effects on GRN activity and SP. Peer reviewers acknowledge these as part of the convincing genetic manipulations demonstrating cell-autonomous and non-autonomous effects.

Perfect agreement on sGRN-specific Ih knockdown effects (C84-C86). Both evaluations find the cell-type specific RNAi data convincing. Peer reviewers note proper controls were added and accept the evidence for HCN's cell-autonomous suppression of sGRN excitability.

Perfect agreement on behavioral validation (C100-C107). Both evaluations strongly support the diet-dependent behavioral findings and their ecological relevance. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the integration of genetic, electrophysiological, and behavioral data as a major strength.

Perfect agreement on non-synaptic mechanism (C108-C114). Both evaluations support the evidence ruling out conventional synaptic transmission. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as providing important new insight into non-synaptic interactions and consider it a major strength of the study.

Perfect agreement on L-type bristle findings (C70-C74). Both evaluations support the extension to water GRNs and third bristle type. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this through noting improvements in sensilla type labeling across figures.

Perfect agreement on HCN's dual functional roles (C128-C130). Both evaluations support the synthesis of context-dependent HCN function. Peer reviewers acknowledge the evolutionary explanation and accept the model of how these interactions impact sensory coding.

Strong agreement on SP measurement methodology (C169-C177). Both evaluations support the technical approach and validation. OpenEval includes C178 about nompC controls while peer review focuses on conceptual illustration improvements. No methodological concerns raised by either.

Strong agreement on diet-dependent SP depletion timecourse (C92-C99). Both evaluations support the experimental findings. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the newly added timecourse data (Fig. 5A-B) and the evolutionary explanation for the system's design.

Agreement on sGRN inactivation effects on bGRN activity (C59-C63). Both evaluations support the genetic and Kir2.1 experiments. Peer reviewers note solid evidence for cross-neuron effects and accept the TNT control ruling out synaptic mechanisms.

Agreement on parallel SP changes with sGRN manipulation (C64-C68). Both evaluations support the correlation between bGRN activity and SP changes. Peer reviewers explicitly state SP measurements support the authors' conclusions about the mechanism.

Agreement on cell-type specificity of HCN requirement (C43-C44, C47-C48). Both evaluations support the Gal4-driver experiments. OpenEval covers broader genetic evidence (C6-C51) while peer review focuses on cell-specific aspects. Peer reviewers note convincing demonstration of cell-autonomous and non-autonomous effects.

Agreement on basic Ih mutant phenotypes (C37, C39, C41). Both evaluations find the genetic evidence convincing. OpenEval covers more extensive claim set (C6-C51) including mechanism and rescue experiments, while peer review focuses on core mutant findings. No concerns raised about basic phenotypes.

Divergent evaluations of RNAi vs mutant discrepancy (C45-C46). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative mechanistic explanation and lack of direct measurements. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, acknowledging the temporal control experiments address developmental concerns, though noting missing temperature controls as a weakness.

Partial overlap on opposing directional effects (C51). OpenEval's broader result (C6-C51) includes this claim as part of supported genetic evidence. Peer review R4 specifically addresses the counterintuitive opposing effects (C49-C52), noting reviewers find them convincing with appropriate discussion.

Related but distinct claims about ectopic HCN temporal dynamics. OpenEval R4 covers gain-of-function effects (C76-C79, C82-C83). Peer R10 addresses temporal analysis improvements (C80-C81) with post-stimulus histograms. Both support ectopic expression findings but focus on different aspects.

Peer review addresses Ih expression pattern controversy (C42) not separately evaluated by OpenEval. Reviewer 3 expresses uncertainty about colocalization interpretation from supplementary data but ultimately accepts the authors' argument that it doesn't affect main conclusions. OpenEval includes C42 context within broader R1 evaluation.

OpenEval evaluates evolutionary speculation (C162-C163) as UNCERTAIN, noting plausible ecological context but lack of direct evidence for adaptive evolution or comparative data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these speculative evolutionary claims.

OpenEval evaluates speculation about HCN in mechanosensory systems (C154-C159) as UNCERTAIN, noting reasonable hypotheses but lack of experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these speculative extensions to mechanosensation.

OpenEval evaluates Kir2.1 mechanistic inferences (C145-C148) as SUPPORTED, noting logical reasoning about membrane potential effects on dendritic signaling despite lack of direct dendritic measurements. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these mechanistic inferences.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background claims (C1-C5, C11-C31) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations for established knowledge about transepithelial potentials, SP depletion, and ephaptic interactions. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate background/introduction claims.

OpenEval evaluates background on mammalian HCN expression and electrophysiology (C115-C127) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these background claims contextualizing the Drosophila findings.

OpenEval evaluates anatomical background on Drosophila gustatory sensilla (C33-C36) as SUPPORTED with proper citations. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these foundational anatomical claims, though they implicitly accept them as context.
